{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABYvVUmg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhCUeTI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 13, "title": "Investigate PC-98/PC-9821 DOS game compatibility with locally downloaded test media", "body": "## Problem

The original-Rust PC-98/PC-9821 Wasm emulator has a useful, but narrowly selected compatibility suite (Star Trail, ADV98, 98VIDEOP, FreeDOS and device-specific guest fixtures). [PR #12](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/12) added IDE, PEGC, mouse and game-driven music, yet a wider selection of independently released **period PC-98 DOS games** has not been systematically exercised. We need to discover the actual incompatibilities and missing hardware/BIOS/CPU behavior **before** proposing speculative feature work.

This Issue is an **investigation and triage task, not a request to implement all missing features**. Register separate, actionable `task` Issues only when failures or concrete missing behavior are demonstrated. Do not open speculative feature requests for hardware that no tested title uses.

## Expected outcome

An AI implementer runs an exploratory compatibility matrix against the current checked-out `main` Rust/Wasm emulator using **legitimately obtainable PC-98/PC-9821 DOS games/software**. Download and execute permitted candidate media **only in the implementer's local development/test environment, outside Git version control and distributable artifacts**. Record compact reproducible observations, isolate genuine emulator problems from unsupported machine profiles/invalid media/guest setup, and file distinct follow-up `task` Issues for verified problems.

Neither the ROM/disk images themselves nor copied game assets are deliverables. PC-98 software will generally be floppy/HDD images or DOS executables rather than firmware ROMs. The research should increase *measured* compatibility and yield developer-actionable diagnoses.

### Test media: license and isolation policy

1. **Check the original publisher/author's actual terms for each specific download before using it.** Freeware/free-to-play, abandonware status, archive availability or an emulator download page do **not** automatically authorize redistribution. Use sources that lawfully offer downloads and permit the intended local testing; obey use/redistribution and other applicable conditions. If permission to obtain/run a candidate is unclear, skip it and choose another one. Do not bypass access controls, DRM or paywalls, or request proprietary BIOS/DOS files.
2. Keep *all downloaded/unpacked original software, disk/HDD images, assets, optional guest OS, save files, and raw sensitive captures* in a clearly separated **local-only ignored directory outside the Git worktree** (preferred), or an explicitly ignored development-only path verified with `git check-ignore`. Never `git add` these files, vendor them, attach them to Issues/PRs, upload them as GitHub Actions artifacts, send them to Pages or include them in a PR diff. Use `git status --short`, `git diff --name-only` and publication packaging checks as appropriate.
3. **Do not send the downloaded game/ROM bytes to hosted CI**, cloud storage, issue attachments or the conversation. Keep this exploratory suite local to the implementing agent. Do not add CI integration tests that need these downloads. Existing checksum-pinned, explicitly redistributable project fixtures and their CI remain unchanged.
4. Issue bodies and any small optional research summary may include original-written diagnostic observations, narrowly scoped textual error reports, game name/version, public source link, legal-use notes, SHA-256 hashes, tested hardware profile, steps, CPU CS:IP/opcode or I/O port/BIOS service identifiers, and descriptive expected-vs-actual behavior. **Exclude copyrighted executable dumps, substantial disassembly, proprietary artwork/audio and unlicensed screenshots.** Do not publish disallowed raw logs or copies of data from tested titles.
5. Local downloads and test media are ephemeral implementation inputs. No requirement to make them downloadable to another agent or reproducible in public CI; document the *legally accessible acquisition path* and concise steps when permitted, but avoid requiring a user or human reviewer to furnish software. Prefer a different freely and lawfully downloadable candidate if one is inaccessible.

### Investigation plan

1. Inspect [current README](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/README.md), [Ap device coverage](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/ap-devices.md), [DOS compatibility boundaries](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md), available tracing/headless commands, existing compatibility fixtures and Issue history. Avoid retesting the same ADV98/98VIDEOP fixtures as if they were new titles.
2. Locate a **diverse set of independent DOS-era PC-98 programs or games** from legitimate sources, ideally six or more distinct titles/versions if lawful downloads permit. Aim for multiple genres and hardware generations (V30/VM versus 286/386/486/9821, Japanese text, 8/16/256 color, FM/OPNA/PCM, FDD/IDE, mouse where available). Prioritize playable games over synthetic diagnostics, and choose only software for which local download/execution is permitted. Record selection/skip reasons and avoid duplicating existing acceptance-only guests.
3. In the implementing environment, download the selected software to isolated local-only paths; record exact source URL, version, license/usage note, acquired file SHA-256, format, prerequisites and machine profile without committing media. Use the emulator's headless runner and/or **locally served actual browser Wasm** to boot or launch the program using a lawfully available guest DOS environment. Ensure disk selection, BIOS/OS requirement, input and sound configuration are correct before attributing a failure to emulation.
4. Explore startup, menu, keyboard/mouse input, multiple frames/scenes, animation/video, audio initiation and game save/reload where applicable. Compare observed behavior against published documentation, known program requirements or other defensible evidence; an unexplained blank screen by itself is not enough to claim a specific missing device. Use bounded deterministic traces/state inspection to identify stops: CS:IP and opcode, unsupported BIOS/IRQ/port, VRAM or palette writes, disk controller status, guest crashes/hangs, timing, etc. Never fake game behavior with host-side compatibility shims.
5. Classify each candidate as **playable**, **partially working**, **fails to boot**, **fails at an identified stage**, or **inconclusive** (e.g., unsupported license/required media or uncertain environment). Note exact tested environment and which aspects were actually verified; avoid claiming broad game support from a single successful boot.
6. For each distinct verified bug or missing capability, create an individual **English `task`-labeled Issue** following the repository template: problem, actual/expected behavior, lawful source and reproduction steps (when shareable), tested profile, diagnosis/evidence, scope of proposed fix and **pre-merge automatable acceptance**. Group multiple games under one Issue when they share a confirmed root cause; avoid duplicate/overlapping tickets. Prefer a small original or openly redistributable micro-fixture that reproduces the underlying hardware defect in CI, without importing any restricted game media. Do not require access to nonredistributable games as a merge condition for those fix Issues. Where no legal CI fixture can be made, clearly document uncertainty and propose an automatable specification-level substitute rather than inventing a test result.
7. On this *research* Issue, add a concise English final comment summarizing the tested matrix (title/version or anonymized identifier when necessary, source/license note, model, outcomes and evidence), any blocked/skipped candidates and links to created follow-up Issues. **Do not create a new Issue for every successful title** and do not perform broad emulator fixes under the investigation Issue. If no actionable defects are reproduced, explicitly report that result rather than filing invented work.

### Development constraints

- Keep the original **no-emulation-libraries** requirement. Investigation may consult publicly available hardware documentation and game usage guides, but no existing emulator's CPU/GDC/OPNA implementation should be copied or ported.
- Focus on **MS-DOS games for PC-9801/PC-9821**. No Windows 3.x/95/98/Win32 game support is requested.
- Keep the current VM and Ap profiles, their tests, and automatic GitHub Pages deployment intact. This research should not add game downloaders to public CI, modify the release artifact or publish unlicensed media.
- Use the [repository development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md). English for Issue titles/bodies and collaboration. No assignee is needed. If only research comments and follow-up Issues are produced, a code PR is unnecessary; use PR review only for actual repository changes.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `main` after PR #12 can boot FreeDOS and selected independent DOS guests. The Ap profile includes partial 386/486 real-mode CPU, 16-/256-color paths, IDE HDD, mouse, FM/OPNA and PCM functionality, but explicitly does not claim complete protected-mode/DPMI/FPU, EGC/GDC, sound-chip or cycle fidelity. See [docs/ap-devices.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/ap-devices.md) and [docs/hardware.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware.md) for exact limitations.

This is a discovery task: failures and unknown compatibility gaps should be *observed*, not guessed. No repository change or commercial test media must be supplied in advance.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

For this research-only Issue, read these as **task completion criteria**; there is no mandatory code merge:

- [ ] Examine current machine profiles, test harnesses and documented known limitations; select a diverse set of independent, legitimately obtainable DOS game/software candidates with per-title license/use notes and without duplicating the existing sample-only suite.
- [ ] Locally execute a meaningful breadth of candidates (target six different programs if suitable lawful inputs exist, with at least three independent playable-game candidates); accurately state the exact count and any license/download/setup barriers rather than manufacturing results to hit a quota.
- [ ] Store all tested external media, downloaded guest OS images, saves and sensitive captures **outside Git tracking**, Pages, PRs, uploaded CI artifacts and issue attachments; report verification that no new restricted data was committed or published.
- [ ] Record a concise compatibility matrix including provenance, hash, machine profile, setup, observed launch/input/video/audio/save behavior and honest pass/partial/fail/inconclusive classification.
- [ ] Diagnose demonstrated failures as far as possible, distinguish emulator defects from bad software/configuration/environment, and open **only actionable new `task` Issues for real problems** with a precise, shareable reproduction and automatable pre-merge acceptance. No speculative issues.
- [ ] Leave an English summary comment on this research Issue with the matrix, findings, links to follow-up Issues, and blocked cases. Do not claim that tests ran until they actually ran; clearly describe gaps.
- [ ] Preserve existing source, tests, GitHub Pages and no-emulation-library policy; no Windows feature implementation. This investigation requires **no human sign-off** or physical hardware.

All completion evidence is obtainable by the AI implementer **before any optional merge**. No licensed media disclosure, human manual playtest, deployment check or post-merge-only action is required.

## Optional validation

Additional games/genres, comparisons to original public behavior descriptions or legally available reference installations, hardware timing checks on personally owned equipment, and future successful fix verification against locally held lawful software. Optional checks must never be human-only merge gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None. This research does not require a merge or production deployment. If a separate fix PR is later merged and a Pages regression appears, open another `task` Issue with an actionable public-environment reproduction.
